issues.title: C86-19 — High: the implementation worker cannot implement or fence files inside submodules
issues.cause: The rewritten prompt emitter still permits only root-worktree Git commands and finishes with a root git add and commit. The workflow's implement-finalize role still snapshots, validates, and diffs only the root occurrence. For a task owning vendor/src/x.ts, root Git cannot stage the contents inside vendor; a submodule-only commit leaves root HEAD unchanged and is rejected; manually advancing the root gitlink makes the fence see only vendor, not vendor/src/x.ts. The apparent end-to-end test manually commits inside the submodule through a callback that the generated worker contract does not provide and declares ownership of vendor rather than the actual nested file.

locations.role: Worker instructions allow only root-worktree Git commands.
Implementation commit and fence validation inspect only the root occurrence.
The deterministic finalizer diffs only the root checkout.
Fixture manually performs the forbidden submodule commit and masks nested ownership behind the root gitlink.

issues.provingTest: Prepare a task whose only owned path is a real file below a submodule. Have the fake worker follow the literal generated instructions, edit that file, and attempt the prescribed commit; the current workflow cannot return done. As a fence negative control, manually commit an unowned file inside the submodule and its root gitlink; a correct implementation reports the normalized nested path, while the current code reports only the gitlink.
suggestedFixApproach: Build an occurrence-aware ownership map. Snapshot, stage, commit, and diff owned paths in each occurrence deepest-first, then commit changed gitlinks in their parents.

Normalize every occurrence-local changed path back to its root-relative task path before fence comparison. Generate explicit git -C <occurrence-checkout> instructions for the worker instead of forbidding them.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: The manifest already supplies occurrence IDs, checkout paths, depths, and parent relationships for occurrence-aware ownership.
Merge already walks occurrences deepest-first and commits changed gitlinks in parents.

acceptanceCriteria: The literal worker contract can stage and commit an owned file below a submodule.
Implementation snapshots and diffs cover every owned occurrence and normalize local paths to root-relative task paths.
An unowned nested edit is reported as the nested path, and focused nested-worktree tests pass.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('implement commits and fences a file owned below a submodule', async () => { /* assert vendor/src/x.ts */ })

issues.title: C86-20 — High: a partial deepest-first merge is misclassified as a zero-progress lap
issues.cause: mergeTaskDeepestFirst may successfully move a source submodule and then fail its parent. The workflow returns the task as failed, recordStageOutcome increments mergedThisLap only for a completely merged task, and shouldEndQueue returns stuck when that count is zero. The spec intentionally keeps earlier source-layer merges, so the retry would not run against the same source state; stopping loses a potentially recoverable task.

locations.role: A child source layer can merge before a later parent layer fails.
A partially completed deepest-first walk is returned as a failed task.
The rewritten workflow forwards the failed merge result without recording source-layer progress.
Queue progress counts only fully merged tasks and declares the partial lap stuck.

issues.provingTest: Use a nested fixture in which the child source merge succeeds and the parent merge fails. Consume the real workflow envelope, prove the child source branch moved, and assert that the current queue has mergedThisLap equal to zero and reports stuck. The corrected queue must begin another lap, subject to the normal lap ceiling, because source progress occurred.
suggestedFixApproach: Track source-layer progress separately from fully merged task count, for example sourceProgressThisLap.
Set it when a failed merge result has a completed layer with status merged, reset it in beginNextLap, and apply the zero-progress exit only when neither a task nor any source layer moved.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: mergeTaskDeepestFirst already retains completedLayers when a later parent layer fails.
The queue already tracks per-lap full-task progress, carryover, and the lap ceiling.

acceptanceCriteria: A failed merge envelope records whether any source layer merged during the attempt.
The queue is stuck only when neither a task nor a source layer moved and failures remain.
beginNextLap resets source progress, and a child-merged/parent-failed regression begins another lap under the existing ceiling.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
return { stage: 'merge', status, completedLayers, parentResult }
// completedLayers retains child layers that moved before the parent failed.

issues.title: C86-21 — High: unexpected rebase/merge exceptions reject the workflow instead of entering the retry queue
issues.cause: The rewrite moved Git and filesystem operations into emitter roles but did not make their failure contract total. A failed merge emitter is retried and eventually becomes the generic merge-driver-no-result envelope, losing the concrete operational reason. A failed rebase-walk or parent-rebase emitter returns no agent result and the workflow explicitly throws, so that stage still rejects with no status/lastFailure envelope for consumeTaskWorkflowResult. The task can therefore remain unqueued and unreported, contrary to tasks 149 and 153.

locations.role: Missing emitter results throw from rebase or degrade to a generic merge failure.
Emitter roles execute throwing rebase, merge, close, ref, and cleanup operations.

issues.provingTest: Make the rebase-walk emitter exit nonzero after a deterministic Git or ref failure and have the workflow agent return no result, as it does when the command produces no valid result instructions. The current workflow retries and then throws instead of returning a blocked envelope. Separately create a leaf ref named refs/taskTools/merge-intents so merge persistence creation fails; the merge path returns only a generic driver-no-result reason. The fixed results must carry the concrete operational reason through queue carryover and reporting. A nested variant should merge the child first and trigger the failure only in the parent, retaining C86-20 progress data.
suggestedFixApproach: Make the rebase and merge primitives total and return typed failure reports, or wrap every stage-level primitive call in try/catch.

Normalize operational exceptions to a nonempty stage-specific lastFailure while preserving completedLayers, source-progress information, conflict paths, and merged-but-not-closed semantics once the root merge has landed.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: concreteMergeStageFailure already converts structured merge failures into nonempty actionable reasons.
Queue consumption already retains ordinary blocked and merged-but-not-closed failures.

acceptanceCriteria: Every rebase-walk, parent-rebase, and merge operational exception becomes a typed workflow result.
lastFailure keeps the concrete operational reason and preserves completed layers, conflicts, source progress, and merged-but-not-closed state.
Queue reporting accepts all normalized failure shapes, including child progress followed by parent failure.

remainingMinimalExample.code: if (!layerWalk) return { stage: 'rebase-test', task: N, status: 'blocked', lastFailure: 'rebase-walk driver returned no result' }

issues.title: C86-22 — High: missingFiles from the third/final plan review is ignored
issues.cause: runPlan performs the first verification, decrements reviewRounds, and handles rejected output only while reviewRounds is greater than zero. It makes three verifier calls but processes only the first two rejections. A third response containing missingFiles exits the loop and implementation begins with the old file fence and unrepaired plan. Task 136 requires widening and replanning whenever verification returns nonempty missingFiles and defines no final-round exception.

locations.role: The loop exits before processing the third verifier rejection.

issues.provingTest: Script verifier responses as rejected with ordinary fixes, rejected with ordinary fixes, then rejected with missingFiles containing b.ts. Assert that the authoritative task record, run-arguments snapshot, rewritten plan and brief, and implementer prompt all include b.ts. They currently do not.
suggestedFixApproach: Model each of the three rounds as verify followed by processing that result.

On a rejected third review, still widen and replan or apply feedback, but do not invoke a fourth verifier. Preserve the final verifier notes and verdict for the user gate so the unverified final repair remains visible.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: widenFilesAndReplan already persists missing files, refreshes the in-memory fence, and replans before another review.
The authoritative widening mutation is already locked and updates the run-arguments snapshot.

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the three review rounds is modeled as verify followed by processing that verifier result.
A final-round missingFiles rejection widens authoritative task state and repairs the plan without invoking a fourth verifier.
Final verifier notes and verdict remain visible to the approval gate when the repaired plan is not reviewed again.

issues.title: C86-23 — High: accepted proposed tasks bypass the task-state lock and can race with close
issues.cause: The gate can invoke create-task while tail workflows are concurrently merging and closing. The generated create-task brief directs its agent to append to tasks.json directly. closeTasks holds the shared lock and publishes a whole-file replacement, but an editor that ignores that lock can overwrite the close or be overwritten by it, resurrecting a closed task or losing the new task.

locations.role: Accepted proposals may invoke create-task while tail workflows are active.
The skill tells an agent to edit tasks.json directly without the task-state mutex.
Close uses a locked whole-file replacement that can race with the unlocked editor.

issues.provingTest: In two real processes, make the append process read tasks.json and pause. Let closeTasks acquire the lock, archive and remove task A, and publish. Resume the stale append of task B and prove A is resurrected. Add the reverse ordering and prove B can be lost under the current direct-editor protocol.
suggestedFixApproach: Add a programmatic task-append command that resolves the authoritative project root, acquires withTaskStateLock, rereads current state, allocates the number, appends, and atomically publishes.
Make the create-task skill gather fields but call that command; it must never write tasks.json directly. Test both orderings with real processes and an acknowledged inside-lock barrier.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: withTaskStateLock and writeJsonAtomically are the established transaction boundary for task-state writers.
Close already rereads and publishes task state while holding that mutex.

acceptanceCriteria: create-task calls one programmatic append operation and never directly edits tasks.json.
Append resolves authoritative state, locks, rereads, allocates, and atomically publishes inside one transaction.
Deterministic real-process tests cover append-first and close-first without resurrection or loss.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
const pair = resolveTaskFiles(projectRoot)
return withTaskStateLock(pair.tasksPath, () => closeTasksLocked(taskNumbers, closureNote, pair, commitHashes))

remainingMinimalExample.code: Send the task draft to appendTask on quoted-heredoc stdin; never edit tasks.json directly.

issues.title: C86-24 — Medium: plan refill can still exceed the shared workflow ceiling after a tail takes the freed slot
issues.cause: The attempted implementation adds total and capacity to nextQueueAction and prevents a tail launch when outstandingEntries is already full. Initial plan/implement launches and refills still happen directly from prose outside that selector. If a plan finishes, an approval's tail takes the freed slot, and the sliding-window instruction then refills the completed plan, the count reaches seven. The new test calls only the tail selector at totals six and five; it never executes the independent plan refill or defines which ready launch owns a freed slot.

locations.role: Plan launches/refills remain direct sliding-window actions while only tail launches call the capacity-aware selector.
nextQueueAction applies total/capacity only when a tail queue step exists and has no representation of a ready plan launch.
The new test directly probes tail launch at two counts and does not drive the plan-refill/tail-launch race or tail-completion allocation.

issues.provingTest: Drive one executable scheduler through six plan launches and a plan completion, then make both a queued approval tail and the next unlaunched plan ready before dispatch. Exercise both event orders and the corresponding tail-completion order while recording every launch and completion. The attempted implementation can launch the tail at total five and then independently refill the plan to seven. The corrected scheduler must choose one launch for the freed slot, never exceed maxConcurrency, enqueue approvals immediately, and keep tail execution serial.
suggestedFixApproach: Represent both the next unlaunched plan and the next tail queue step in one capacity-aware action selector; neither the initial sliding window nor a refill may launch outside it.
Choose and document deterministic priority when both are ready, then test plan-completion, approval, and tail-completion event orders through the same executable scheduler.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: nextQueueAction is already the executable selector for serial tail launch, wait, lap rollover, and reporting.
The emitted instructions already track outstandingEntries across plan/implement and tail workflows.

acceptanceCriteria: One capacity decision covers every plan/implement, rebase-test, and merge launch.
A freed slot is assigned exactly once when a plan refill and an approved tail are both ready; no event order exceeds maxConcurrency and tail execution remains serial.
Executable scheduler tests cover plan-completion, approval, and tail-completion slot allocation while approvals remain immediately enqueueable.

issues.cause: The emitter's loadPreparedTask resolves and reads tasks.json under WORKTREE. Widening correctly updates authoritative state under SOURCE_ROOT and briefly writes a widened worktree brief, but the next plan or verify role calls loadPreparedTask again, reloads the stale private task record, overwrites the widened brief, and emits the old ownership list. The workflow's in-memory preparedTask.files update is not passed to the emitter. A separately launched implement stage has the same stale-fence defect.

The current plan role reloads the private a.ts-only record and overwrites the widened brief. Also launch a fresh implement stage and assert that its prompt and returned fence include b.ts; current behavior reloads only a.ts.

The task can therefore merge changes outside its approved fence after the approval gate.

issues.title: C86-28 — Medium: cleanup failure is reported but has no production cleanup-only retry
issues.cause: The attempted implementation now retains persistence until cleanup succeeds and carries cleanup-incomplete through queue reporting. It does not provide a production action or workflow role that consumes that record and retries cleanup. The locked-worktree test unlocks and manually calls low-level cleanup functions, never releases the task worktree lease, never clears queue.cleanupIncomplete, and never proves the emitted orchestrator can invoke the retry. The skill text also reports only unmerged and mergedNotClosed outcomes, so the new cleanupIncomplete report is not handed to the user as actionable work.

locations.role: The merge role emits cleanup-incomplete and releases the lease only on immediate success, but exposes no cleanup-only retry role.
The queue records cleanupIncomplete permanently but has no retry action or transition that clears a successfully cleaned record.
The emitted driver neither handles cleanup-incomplete nor reports that section to the user.
The retry is performed manually with low-level primitives and omits lease release and queue/report clearing.

issues.provingTest: Force worktree deletion to fail after merge and close, consume the real envelope, and assert the report names the actual retained worktree, branches, persistence refs, and lease. Unlock it and invoke the production cleanup-only entry point advertised by the emitted workflow. The attempted implementation has no such entry point. A correct retry removes every artifact, deletes persistence and the lease last, removes the cleanupIncomplete queue record, produces an empty follow-up warning report, and remains idempotent when invoked again.
suggestedFixApproach: Keep the new persistence ordering and cleanupIncomplete reporting, but add an explicit cleanup-only workflow role/action that receives the retained task context and cannot re-run merge or close.
Have a successful retry remove worktrees and branches across occurrences, delete persistence and the owner lease last, and transition the queue by removing that task's cleanupIncomplete record.
Teach the emitted orchestrator to report and invoke this action, and derive retainedArtifacts from actual remaining paths/refs instead of a partial static list.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: MergedNotClosedTask and buildMergeReport already preserve merges whose archival step failed.
The merge role already separates merge, close, persistence, and final cleanup and returns cleanupWarning.

acceptanceCriteria: Merge persistence remains until worktree and branch cleanup succeeds.
Cleanup failure creates a reported cleanupIncomplete record with warning and retained artifact paths.
The emitted production workflow can invoke an idempotent cleanup-only retry without re-merging or re-closing the task.
A successful retry removes all occurrence artifacts, persistence, and the lease in safe order and clears cleanupIncomplete from the next report.

issues.title: C86-29 — Medium: the new worktree lease is not lifecycle-safe or explicitly recoverable
issues.cause: The attempted implementation atomically creates a per-worktree lease before reset or creation, so a sequential second call is rejected. Acquisition is not wrapped around preparation cleanup: checkout, worktree add, submodule initialization, or branch creation failures leave an orphan lease. The stored runId is generated inside the lease rather than using the workflow's runId, and releaseTaskWorktreeLease is an unconditional unlink with no owner check or retained-work verification. Its test calls createWorktreeForGroup twice in one process without a barrier, so it does not prove two live preparation processes cannot race, and there is no safe explicit stale-lease recovery operation.

locations.role: Lease acquisition is atomic, but failure cleanup, ownership-checked release, actual run identity, and safe stale recovery are absent.
Only the immediate successful merge path releases the lease; no recovery path safely releases it after failed preparation or cleanup.
The ownership test is sequential and same-process, while the existing preparation-failure case does not assert that its acquired lease is released.

issues.provingTest: Start two real prepare processes for the same task behind a barrier immediately before exclusive acquisition. Exactly one must acquire the lease carrying its real runId, and the loser must fail without resetting or sharing the checkout. Separately force worktree-add and submodule-initialization failures and assert their lease is released. Finally create a stale lease plus retained work: ordinary preparation must refuse it, and the explicit recovery operation must preserve/report the work and require matching ownership or deliberate takeover before releasing the lease.
suggestedFixApproach: Keep atomic wx acquisition, but pass the actual workflow run/session identity into it and return an owner token used by every release.
Wrap all post-acquisition preparation in try/catch/finally so a failed preparation releases only its own lease, while a successful preparation transfers lease ownership to final cleanup.
Add an explicit stale-lease recovery operation that reads identity, checks owner liveness as appropriate, inspects retained work, and preserves or reports that work before any deliberate takeover.
Replace the sequential unit test with deterministic child processes synchronized at an acquisition barrier, and cover preparation-failure cleanup and stale recovery.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: worktreeHoldsRetainedWork already prevents automatic reuse from destroying commits or dirty edits left for recovery.
The task-state mutex demonstrates the repository's existing atomic exclusive-create lease primitive and fail-safe timeout behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: Preparation atomically acquires an exclusive per-task live-run lease before resetting or creating the worktree.
A concurrent preparation for the same task fails without resetting, modifying, or sharing the first run's checkout.
The lease records the actual run/session identity, ownership-checked release occurs after successful final cleanup, and failed preparation does not leave an orphan lease.
Stale-lease recovery is explicit and preserves retained work; barrier-synchronized real-process tests deterministically prove single ownership and recovery behavior.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
const fd = openSync(leasePath, 'wx', 0o600)
writeFileSync(fd, JSON.stringify({ pid: process.pid, runId: generateRunId(), createdAt: Date.now() }))

remainingMinimalExample.code:

test('failed preparation releases only its lease', () => { /* worktree add and submodule init failures */ })
test('stale recovery preserves retained work', () => { /* explicit takeover */ })

A missing expected plan returns needs-clarification before verifier or implementer agents run.
Both missing-expected-path and wrong-existing-path regressions pass while the workflow remains import-free.

issues.title: C86-36 — High: retryAgent re-executes mutating emitter roles after their side effects have already landed
issues.cause: The rewrite routes deterministic mutations through agent calls and wraps every call in retryAgent. retryAgent cannot distinguish a command that failed before mutation from an agent that successfully ran the command but was killed or returned null before relaying its structured result. It therefore executes the same mutation again. The merge role can merge, close the task, delete persistence, and remove the worktree on its first attempt; a lost agent result then reruns against a deleted worktree and finally reports the task blocked even though it was already merged and closed. advance-conflict can similarly continue a rebase once and then retry against a no-longer-active rebase. Tests immediately parse and return emitter output, so none model result loss after command completion.

locations.role: The common retry wrapper is applied to mutating conflict, rebase, and merge driver roles.
These roles commit, continue or abort rebases, merge, close, delete refs, and remove worktrees before printing their result.
Harness always converts successful emitter stdout directly into the agent result and cannot simulate a lost result after mutation.

issues.provingTest: Drive a real merge-stage fixture with an agent wrapper that executes the merge emitter command on attempt one but discards its stdout and returns null. Let retryAgent launch attempt two. The current first attempt merges and closes the task; later attempts fail because cleanup removed the worktree, and the workflow reports blocked or no result despite completed state. Add the analogous advance-conflict case where the first command successfully continues the rebase but its agent result is lost.
suggestedFixApproach: Do not blindly retry a mutating role. Give each mutation an idempotency key and persist its typed result atomically before printing it, or split mutation from result retrieval so retries call a read-only receipt/status role.

For merge, record a run/task/stage receipt before returning and have repeated invocations return that receipt without re-running merge, close, or cleanup. For conflict continuation, persist or derive a reconciled state that distinguishes already-continued from never-started.

Extend the harness so the real emitter command can complete while the enclosing agent returns null. Assert that retry obtains the original receipt, performs no second mutation, and reports the actual final state.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: retryAgent correctly retries missing results for read-only prompt and status roles and preserves valid falsy results.
Mutating roles are already centralized behind named emitter dispatch points, which provides a place to add idempotency keys and durable receipts.

acceptanceCriteria: Mutating emitter roles are never blindly executed a second time after their first attempt may have committed side effects.
Each mutation has an idempotency key and persists its typed result before returning output, or retries use a read-only receipt/status role.
A lost merge result is recovered as the original merged/closed outcome without a second merge, close, persistence deletion, or cleanup attempt.
A lost advance-conflict result is reconciled without continuing or aborting the rebase twice, while ordinary read-only retries retain current behavior.
